title: No-thought
hook: Huineng: no-thought is not blankness but not being stuck to thoughts

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Platform Sutra: a woodcutter from the south who became, as tradition calls him, the sixth patriarch. Buddha-nature has no north or south. Where did that answer come in handy? Day one thousand two hundred seventeen.

A big station has a departures board. Every few minutes it clicks over: a new train, a new platform, a new city. Nobody standing in the hall gets on every train. Most people glance up, read a line, and keep walking. Some trains they board. Most they let go, and the board doesn't mind either way. Now try the same thing with a mind. Thoughts click over all day. Lunch. That email. A song from years ago. A worry about Thursday. Huineng had a word for meeting them the way a traveler meets a departures board, and it is probably not what it sounds like. Today: no-thought.
screen: `A DEPARTURES BOARD.` → `NOBODY BOARDS EVERY TRAIN.` → `THOUGHTS CLICK OVER ALL DAY.`

segments.voice: First, where the word sits. In the Platform Sutra, Huineng sets out three teachings side by side: no-thought as the doctrine, no-form as the substance, and non-abiding as the root. Today we take the first, but they lean on each other. Second, what no-thought is not. It sounds like an empty head, a mind wiped blank. Huineng says plainly that this is a mistake. Trying to think of nothing at all, cutting off every thought, is in his telling its own kind of trap, a mind tied up by an idea of what meditation should be. Third, what it is. In paraphrase, he says no-thought means that in the midst of thoughts, you are not carried off by them. Thought follows thought, and none of them is held on to. That is the non-abiding: the mind doesn't move in and live in any one of them. When thoughts don't stick, he says, there is no bondage. So the thought about Thursday can arrive, and can even be useful, and then go, the way a train leaves the board. Fourth, the senses stay open. Huineng doesn't ask anyone to close their eyes on the world. He describes the senses going out and coming back freely, seeing and hearing everything, while the mind isn't stained by what it meets. No-thought, in his hands, is not less life. It is full life, with nothing gripping. This is the same thread the Xinxin Ming was pulling a few days ago, now tied to a teacher's seat: not stuck.
screen: `THREE TEACHINGS, ONE STRAND.` · `NOT A BLANK MIND.` · `THOUGHT AFTER THOUGHT, UNSTUCK.` · `THE SENSES COME AND GO FREELY.` · then, large: `NOT STUCK.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like. Sit and let the breath settle. Don't try to stop thinking. Let thoughts come, the way lines come up on a departures board. When one appears, notice it: there's a thought. Then let it go on without you. If you find you've boarded one, and you're a few stops down the line in a story, that's fine. Just step off and come back to the breath. Later today, if you have five minutes, try it again for the whole five. The bell holds the time.
No-thought. Huineng's teaching that the mind can meet every thought without being carried off by any of them. Not blankness. Today's word.
Your line: not stuck. Today, when a thought keeps circling, let it arrive and leave once without boarding it. Day one thousand two hundred seventeen.

howItsDone: Zen and Chan teachers often explain Huineng's no-thought in talks on sitting, describing practice as letting thoughts arise and pass without being carried off, rather than forcing the mind blank.

myth: for Huineng, no-thought means stopping all thinking
he says it means not being carried off by thoughts, and warns against forcing the mind blank.
Huineng pairs no-thought with no-form and non-abiding
he sets the three side by side as doctrine, substance and root.
no-thought means closing off the senses
he describes the senses going out and coming back freely, with the mind unstained.

fork.setup: you're sitting, and a worry about Thursday's meeting shows up. by Huineng's teaching, what now?
options: shove it out and make the mind blank
let it arrive and go without boarding it
follow it all the way to the end to be done with it
fork.reveal: Huineng calls forcing the mind blank a mistake. no-thought is meeting the thought without being carried off.

original.note: Chinese (wunian): 'no-thought', the first of Huineng's three teachings in the Platform Sutra.

trapdoor: what you thought: no-thought means emptying your head.
what it means: thoughts arise and pass, and the mind isn't stuck to any of them.
what a scholar hears: Huineng sets 無念, no-thought, beside no-form and non-abiding, and explains it as not being carried off in the midst of thought, not the end of thinking.

sources.ref: Platform Sutra, the teaching on no-thought, no-form and non-abiding
sources.work: The Platform Sutra of the Sixth Patriarch

notes: Check against the Chinese: 無念為宗，無相為體，無住為本; 'in the midst of thought, not thinking' (於念而無念); thought after thought not abiding means no bondage; the warning against cutting off all thought; senses coming and going freely without being stained.
